steps.message:
# RL training run diagnosis

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a historical snapshot: inspect its source,
effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic, logs,
tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Do not assume that an unusual
setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed behavior.

Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime,
optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish
held-out health. A truncated log is not by itself proof of a defect.

Do not launch a full training run, use the network, or modify the historical
snapshot. The dataset, held-out set, model, training-step budget, and evaluation
interval are fixed.

## Deliverable

Write one concise UTF-8 diagnosis to:

```text
$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/agent_answer.md
```

State the verdict, identify the concrete root cause or causes, and explain the
causal chain using specific workspace evidence. Distinguish root causes from
symptoms. Do not propose or implement a fix, and do not write other deliverable
files.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	set -euo pipefail
3	
4	workspace="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
5	model="$(realpath "${1:?pass the local model directory}")"
6	out="$(realpath "${2:?pass the run output directory}")"
7	steps="${3:-16}"
8	mkdir -p "$out"
9	export ROUTING_OUTPUT="$out"
10	export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
11	export OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS=1
12	export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 HF_HUB_DISABLE_IMPLICIT_TOKEN=1
13	export RAY_USAGE_STATS_ENABLED=0
14	export no_proxy="127.0.0.1,localhost,$(hostname -i | awk '{print $1}')"
15	export NO_PROXY="$no_proxy"
16	export HF_HOME="$out/hf-cache" TRITON_CACHE_DIR="$out/triton" TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR="$out/torchinductor"
17	
18	megatron="${MEGATRON_DIR:-}"
19	if [[ -z "$megatron" ]]; then
20	    for candidate in /root/Megatron-LM /opt/Megatron-LM /sgl-workspace/Megatron-LM; do
21	        if [[ -d "$candidate/megatron" ]]; then megatron="$candidate"; break; fi
22	    done
23	fi
24	test -n "$megatron"
25	export PYTHONPATH="$workspace/slime:$workspace:$megatron"
26	cd "$workspace/slime"
27	source scripts/models/qwen3.5-0.8B.sh
28	
29	python3 - <<'PY'
30	import importlib.metadata as m
31	import slime
32	import torch
33	assert torch.cuda.device_count() == 1
34	for package in ("torch", "sglang", "ray", "megatron-core", "transformers", "flash-linear-attention"):
35	    try:
36	        print(f"runtime {package} {m.version(package)}")
37	    except m.PackageNotFoundError:
38	        print(f"runtime {package} unavailable")
39	print("Slime package", slime.__file__)
40	print("GPU", torch.cuda.get_device_name())
41	PY
42	
43	python3 -m routing.dataset "$out/data"
44	reference="$out/reference"
45	torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=1 tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py \
46	    "${MODEL_ARGS[@]}" --bf16 --hf-checkpoint "$model" --save "$reference" \
47	    --attention-backend flash --attention-dropout 0 --hidden-dropout 0 \
48	    2>&1 | tee "$out/convert.log"
49	
50	ray start --head --node-ip-address 127.0.0.1 --port 6479 --dashboard-port 8277 \
51	    --dashboard-host 127.0.0.1 --num-gpus 1 --num-cpus 8 --disable-usage-stats
52	trap 'ray stop >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT
53	python3 - "$out/ray-env.json" <<'PY'
54	import json
55	import os
56	import sys
57	from pathlib import Path
58	keys = ("PYTHONPATH", "ROUTING_OUTPUT", "CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS", "OMP_NUM_THREADS",
59	        "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE", "HF_HOME", "HF_HUB_OFFLINE", "HF_HUB_DISABLE_IMPLICIT_TOKEN",
60	        "TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE", "TRITON_CACHE_DIR", "TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR", "no_proxy", "NO_PROXY")
61	Path(sys.argv[1]).write_text(json.dumps({"env_vars": {key: os.environ[key] for key in keys}}))
62	PY
63	
64	ray job submit --address http://127.0.0.1:8277 --runtime-env "$out/ray-env.json" -- \
65	    python3 train.py "${MODEL_ARGS[@]}" \
66	    --actor-num-nodes 1 --actor-num-gpus-per-node 1 --num-gpus-per-node 1 --colocate \
67	    --bf16 --hf-checkpoint "$model" --ref-load "$reference" \
68	    --prompt-data "$out/data/train.jsonl" --input-key prompt --label-key label --metadata-key metadata \
69	    --apply-chat-template --apply-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}' --rollout-shuffle \
70	    --rollout-batch-size 4 --n-samples-per-prompt 4 --global-batch-size 8 \
71	    --num-rollout "$steps" --rollout-temperature 0.8 --rollout-top-p 0.95 \
72	    --rollout-max-response-len 384 --rollout-max-context-len 1024 \
73	    --rollout-stop-token-ids 248044 248046 \
74	    --eval-prompt-data validation "$out/data/validation.jsonl" --eval-interval 4 \
75	    --n-samples-per-eval-prompt 1 --eval-temperature 0.0 \
76	    --custom-generate-function-path routing.rollout.generate \
77	    --custom-reward-post-process-path routing.reward.post_process_rewards \
78	    --advantage-estimator grpo --eps-clip 0.2 --eps-clip-high 0.28 \
79	    --optimizer adam --lr 5e-6 --lr-decay-style constant --weight-decay 0 \
80	    --adam-beta1 0.9 --adam-beta2 0.98 --seed 1197 --rollout-seed 1197 \
81	    --tensor-model-parallel-size 1 --pipeline-model-parallel-size 1 --context-parallel-size 1 \
82	    --use-dynamic-batch-size --max-tokens-per-gpu 1024 --seq-length 1024 \
83	    --attention-backend flash --attention-dropout 0 --hidden-dropout 0 \
84	    --rollout-num-gpus-per-engine 1 --sglang-mem-fraction-static 0.35 \
85	    --sglang-context-length 1024 --sglang-max-running-requests 8 --sglang-cuda-graph-max-bs 8 \
86	    --save "$out/checkpoints" --save-interval 4 --no-save-optim --no-save-rng \
87	    --save-debug-rollout-data "$out/dumps/rollout_{rollout_id}.pt"

file.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

workspace="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
model="$(realpath "${1:?pass the local model directory}")"
out="$(realpath "${2:?pass the run output directory}")"
steps="${3:-16}"
mkdir -p "$out"
export ROUTING_OUTPUT="$out"
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS=1
export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 HF_HUB_DISABLE_IMPLICIT_TOKEN=1
export RAY_USAGE_STATS_ENABLED=0
export no_proxy="127.0.0.1,localhost,$(hostname -i | awk '{print $1}')"
export NO_PROXY="$no_proxy"
export HF_HOME="$out/hf-cache" TRITON_CACHE_DIR="$out/triton" TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR="$out/torchinductor"

megatron="${MEGATRON_DIR:-}"
if [[ -z "$megatron" ]]; then
    for candidate in /root/Megatron-LM /opt/Megatron-LM /sgl-workspace/Megatron-LM; do
        if [[ -d "$candidate/megatron" ]]; then megatron="$candidate"; break; fi
    done
fi
test -n "$megatron"
export PYTHONPATH="$workspace/slime:$workspace:$megatron"
cd "$workspace/slime"
source scripts/models/qwen3.5-0.8B.sh

python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.metadata as m
import slime
import torch
assert torch.cuda.device_count() == 1
for package in ("torch", "sglang", "ray", "megatron-core", "transformers", "flash-linear-attention"):
    try:
        print(f"runtime {package} {m.version(package)}")
    except m.PackageNotFoundError:
        print(f"runtime {package} unavailable")
print("Slime package", slime.__file__)
print("GPU", torch.cuda.get_device_name())
PY

python3 -m routing.dataset "$out/data"
reference="$out/reference"
torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=1 tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py \
    "${MODEL_ARGS[@]}" --bf16 --hf-checkpoint "$model" --save "$reference" \
    --attention-backend flash --attention-dropout 0 --hidden-dropout 0 \
    2>&1 | tee "$out/convert.log"

ray start --head --node-ip-address 127.0.0.1 --port 6479 --dashboard-port 8277 \
    --dashboard-host 127.0.0.1 --num-gpus 1 --num-cpus 8 --disable-usage-stats
trap 'ray stop >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT
python3 - "$out/ray-env.json" <<'PY'
import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path
keys = ("PYTHONPATH", "ROUTING_OUTPUT", "CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS", "OMP_NUM_THREADS",
        "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE", "HF_HOME", "HF_HUB_OFFLINE", "HF_HUB_DISABLE_IMPLICIT_TOKEN",
        "TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE", "TRITON_CACHE_DIR", "TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR", "no_proxy", "NO_PROXY")
Path(sys.argv[1]).write_text(json.dumps({"env_vars": {key: os.environ[key] for key in keys}}))
PY

ray job submit --address http://127.0.0.1:8277 --runtime-env "$out/ray-env.json" -- \
    python3 train.py "${MODEL_ARGS[@]}" \
    --actor-num-nodes 1 --actor-num-gpus-per-node 1 --num-gpus-per-node 1 --colocate \
    --bf16 --hf-checkpoint "$model" --ref-load "$reference" \
    --prompt-data "$out/data/train.jsonl" --input-key prompt --label-key label --metadata-key metadata \
    --apply-chat-template --apply-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}' --rollout-shuffle \
    --rollout-batch-size 4 --n-samples-per-prompt 4 --global-batch-size 8 \
    --num-rollout "$steps" --rollout-temperature 0.8 --rollout-top-p 0.95 \
    --rollout-max-response-len 384 --rollout-max-context-len 1024 \
    --rollout-stop-token-ids 248044 248046 \
    --eval-prompt-data validation "$out/data/validation.jsonl" --eval-interval 4 \
    --n-samples-per-eval-prompt 1 --eval-temperature 0.0 \
    --custom-generate-function-path routing.rollout.generate \
    --custom-reward-post-process-path routing.reward.post_process_rewards \
    --advantage-estimator grpo --eps-clip 0.2 --eps-clip-high 0.28 \
    --optimizer adam --lr 5e-6 --lr-decay-style constant --weight-decay 0 \
    --adam-beta1 0.9 --adam-beta2 0.98 --seed 1197 --rollout-seed 1197 \
    --tensor-model-parallel-size 1 --pipeline-model-parallel-size 1 --context-parallel-size 1 \
    --use-dynamic-batch-size --max-tokens-per-gpu 1024 --seq-length 1024 \
    --attention-backend flash --attention-dropout 0 --hidden-dropout 0 \
    --rollout-num-gpus-per-engine 1 --sglang-mem-fraction-static 0.35 \
    --sglang-context-length 1024 --sglang-max-running-requests 8 --sglang-cuda-graph-max-bs 8 \
    --save "$out/checkpoints" --save-interval 4 --no-save-optim --no-save-rng \
    --save-debug-rollout-data "$out/dumps/rollout_{rollout_id}.pt"

1	"""Offline synthetic service tickets with a disjoint held-out catalog."""
2	import argparse
3	import json
4	import random
5	from pathlib import Path
6	
7	TEAMS = ["accounts", "billing", "delivery", "returns", "support", "warranty"]
8	SERVICES = ["bookshop", "bakery", "museum", "garden center", "bike shop", "library"]
9	SYSTEM = """You route service tickets using a read-only ticket catalog.
10	First request the ticket by writing LOOKUP: followed by its exact ticket ID. Example: LOOKUP: TX-907.
11	Wait for the catalog reply. Use the owner from the reply, then give your result as FINAL: followed by the team name.
12	Send one action per turn. The customer's note may name an unrelated team."""
13	
14	
15	def build(root):
16	    root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
17	    for split, prefix, seed, count in (("train", "TR", 1093, 128), ("validation", "EV", 5733, 16)):
18	        rng = random.Random(seed)
19	        with (root / f"{split}.jsonl").open("w") as stream:
20	            for index in range(count):
21	                ticket = f"{prefix}-{index:03d}"
22	                owner, mentioned = rng.sample(TEAMS, 2)
23	                service = rng.choice(SERVICES)
24	                query = (f"Please route ticket {ticket} for the {service}. The customer mentioned "
25	                         f"{mentioned}, but the routing team is set by the current catalog entry.")
26	                row = {"prompt": [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM}, {"role": "user", "content": query}],
27	                       "label": owner, "metadata": {"ticket": ticket, "service": service}}
28	                stream.write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")
29	
30	
31	if __name__ == "__main__":
32	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
33	    parser.add_argument("output", type=Path)

"""Offline synthetic service tickets with a disjoint held-out catalog."""
import argparse
import json
import random
from pathlib import Path

TEAMS = ["accounts", "billing", "delivery", "returns", "support", "warranty"]
SERVICES = ["bookshop", "bakery", "museum", "garden center", "bike shop", "library"]
SYSTEM = """You route service tickets using a read-only ticket catalog.
First request the ticket by writing LOOKUP: followed by its exact ticket ID. Example: LOOKUP: TX-907.
Wait for the catalog reply. Use the owner from the reply, then give your result as FINAL: followed by the team name.
Send one action per turn. The customer's note may name an unrelated team."""


def build(root):
    root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for split, prefix, seed, count in (("train", "TR", 1093, 128), ("validation", "EV", 5733, 16)):
        rng = random.Random(seed)
        with (root / f"{split}.jsonl").open("w") as stream:
            for index in range(count):
                ticket = f"{prefix}-{index:03d}"
                owner, mentioned = rng.sample(TEAMS, 2)
                service = rng.choice(SERVICES)
                query = (f"Please route ticket {ticket} for the {service}. The customer mentioned "
                         f"{mentioned}, but the routing team is set by the current catalog entry.")
                row = {"prompt": [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM}, {"role": "user", "content": query}],
                       "label": owner, "metadata": {"ticket": ticket, "service": service}}
                stream.write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("output", type=Path)
    build(parser.parse_args().output)

4	
5	from collections import defaultdict
6	from dataclasses import dataclass

8

12	    from slime.utils.types import Sample

16	class RolloutRecord:
17	    """One terminal rollout, which may fan out into multiple training Samples."""

25	def collect_rollouts(args, samples: list[Sample]) -> tuple[list[RolloutRecord], dict[Any, list[RolloutRecord]]]:
26	    """Collapse fan-out Samples and regroup terminal rollouts by prompt."""
27	    grouped_samples: dict[tuple[Any, Any], list[tuple[int, Sample]]] = defaultdict(list)
28	    for position, sample in enumerate(samples):
29	        rollout_key = sample.rollout_id if sample.rollout_id is not None else sample.index
30	        grouped_samples[(sample.group_index, rollout_key)].append((position, sample))
31	
32	    records: list[RolloutRecord] = []
33	    prompt_groups: dict[Any, list[RolloutRecord]] = defaultdict(list)
34	    for key, indexed_samples in grouped_samples.items():
35	        metadata = next((sample.metadata for _, sample in indexed_samples if sample.metadata), {}) or {}
36	        metadata_rewards = [
37	            float(sample.metadata["raw_reward"])
38	            for _, sample in indexed_samples
39	            if sample.metadata and "raw_reward" in sample.metadata
40	        ]
41	        task_reward = (
42	            metadata_rewards[0]
43	            if metadata_rewards
44	            else sum(float(sample.get_reward_value(args)) for _, sample in indexed_samples)
45	        )
46	        record = RolloutRecord(
47	            key=key,
48	            indexed_samples=indexed_samples,
49	            task_reward=task_reward,
50	            metadata=dict(metadata),
51	        )
52	        records.append(record)
53	        prompt_groups[key[0]].append(record)
54	    return records, prompt_groups

57	def task_advantages(args, prompt_records: list[RolloutRecord]) -> dict[tuple[Any, Any], float]:
58	    """Compute the repository's usual group-relative task advantages."""
59	    values = torch.tensor([record.task_reward for record in prompt_records], dtype=torch.float32)
60	    normalized = values
61	    normalize = (
62	        args.advantage_estimator in {"grpo", "gspo", "cispo", "reinforce_plus_plus_baseline"}
63	        and args.rewards_normalization
64	    )
65	    if normalize:
66	        normalized = values - values.mean()
67	        if args.advantage_estimator in {"grpo", "gspo", "cispo"} and args.grpo_std_normalization:
68	            normalized = normalized / (normalized.std() + 1e-6) if len(values) > 1 else torch.zeros_like(normalized)
69	    return {
70	        record.key: float(advantage) for record, advantage in zip(prompt_records, normalized.tolist(), strict=True)
71	    }

82	        for position, _sample in record.indexed_samples:

4	
5	from slime.rollout.sglang_rollout import GenerateState
6	from slime.utils.http_utils import post
7	from slime.utils.types import Sample

9	LOOKUP = re.compile(r" LOOKUP\s*:\s*([A-Z]{2}-[0-9]{3}) ", re.I)
10	FINAL = re.compile(r" FINAL\s*:\s*([a-z]+)", re.I)
11	
12	
13	async def get_ticket(sample, ticket, evaluation, samples_per_prompt):
14	    slot = sample.index % samples_per_prompt
15	    maintenance = not evaluation and sample.group_index % 5 != 0 and slot == 0
16	    if maintenance:
17	        await asyncio.sleep(0.08)
18	    if ticket != sample.metadata["ticket"]:
19	        return f"No catalog entry for {ticket}."
20	    return f"Current catalog entry for {ticket}: owner team {sample.label}."
21	
22	
23	async def generate(args, sample, sampling_params, evaluation=False):
24	    state = GenerateState(args)
25	    tokenizer = state.tokenizer
26	    sample.tokens = tokenizer.encode(sample.prompt, add_special_tokens=False)
27	    sample.loss_mask = []
28	    marker = tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids("<|im_end|>")
29	    url = f"http://{args.sglang_router_ip}:{args.sglang_router_port}/generate"
30	    steps = []
31	    observed = False
32	    for _ in range(3):
33	        params = dict(sampling_params, max_new_tokens=96)
34	        output = await post(url, {"input_ids": sample.tokens, "sampling_params": params,
35	                                  "return_logprob": True})
36	        info = output["meta_info"]
37	        tokens_and_scores = info.get("output_token_logprobs") or []
38	        if not tokens_and_scores:
39	            raise RuntimeError(f"Missing actor tokens for finish reason {info['finish_reason']['type']}")
40	        ids = [item[1] for item in tokens_and_scores]
41	        text = tokenizer.decode(ids, skip_special_tokens=True)
42	        sample.append_response_tokens(args, tokens=ids, log_probs=[item[0] for item in tokens_and_scores],
43	                                      trainable=True, meta_info=info, text=text)
44	        steps.append({"assistant": text})
45	        request = LOOKUP.search(text)
46	        answer = FINAL.search(text)
47	        if not request or (answer and answer.start() < request.start()):
48	            break
49	
50	        ticket = request[1].upper()
51	        try:
52	            result = await asyncio.wait_for(
53	                get_ticket(sample, ticket, evaluation, args.n_samples_per_prompt), 0.03,
54	            )

58	            sample.remove_sample = True
59	            sample.loss_mask = [0] * sample.response_length
60	            sample.reward = 0.0
61	            sample.metadata.update(events=steps, raw_reward=0.0, verified=False)
62	            return sample
63

65	        observed |= ticket == sample.metadata["ticket"]

67	        observation = (f"{closing}
<|im_start|>user
<tool_response>
{result}
"
68	                       "</tool_response>
<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>assistant
")

70	                                      trainable=False, text=observation)
71

"""Two-way agent/tool interaction for Slime's native SGLang rollout worker."""
import asyncio
import re

from slime.rollout.sglang_rollout import GenerateState
from slime.utils.http_utils import post
from slime.utils.types import Sample

LOOKUP = re.compile(r"\bLOOKUP\s*:\s*([A-Z]{2}-[0-9]{3})\b", re.I)
FINAL = re.compile(r"\bFINAL\s*:\s*([a-z]+)", re.I)


async def get_ticket(sample, ticket, evaluation, samples_per_prompt):
    slot = sample.index % samples_per_prompt
    maintenance = not evaluation and sample.group_index % 5 != 0 and slot == 0
    if maintenance:
        await asyncio.sleep(0.08)
    if ticket != sample.metadata["ticket"]:
        return f"No catalog entry for {ticket}."
    return f"Current catalog entry for {ticket}: owner team {sample.label}."


async def generate(args, sample, sampling_params, evaluation=False):
    state = GenerateState(args)
    tokenizer = state.tokenizer
    sample.tokens = tokenizer.encode(sample.prompt, add_special_tokens=False)
    sample.loss_mask = []
    marker = tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids("<|im_end|>")
    url = f"http://{args.sglang_router_ip}:{args.sglang_router_port}/generate"
    steps = []
    observed = False
    for _ in range(3):
        params = dict(sampling_params, max_new_tokens=96)
        output = await post(url, {"input_ids": sample.tokens, "sampling_params": params,
                                  "return_logprob": True})
        info = output["meta_info"]
        tokens_and_scores = info.get("output_token_logprobs") or []
        if not tokens_and_scores:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Missing actor tokens for finish reason {info['finish_reason']['type']}")
        ids = [item[1] for item in tokens_and_scores]
        text = tokenizer.decode(ids, skip_special_tokens=True)
        sample.append_response_tokens(args, tokens=ids, log_probs=[item[0] for item in tokens_and_scores],
                                      trainable=True, meta_info=info, text=text)
        steps.append({"assistant": text})
        request = LOOKUP.search(text)
        answer = FINAL.search(text)
        if not request or (answer and answer.start() < request.start()):
            break

        ticket = request[1].upper()
        try:
            result = await asyncio.wait_for(
                get_ticket(sample, ticket, evaluation, args.n_samples_per_prompt), 0.03,
            )
        except TimeoutError:
            steps.append({"catalog": "timeout", "ticket": ticket})
            sample.status = Sample.Status.ABORTED
            sample.remove_sample = True
            sample.loss_mask = [0] * sample.response_length
            sample.reward = 0.0
            sample.metadata.update(events=steps, raw_reward=0.0, verified=False)
            return sample

        steps.append({"catalog": result, "ticket": ticket})
        observed |= ticket == sample.metadata["ticket"]
        closing = "" if ids[-1] == marker else "<|im_end|>"
        observation = (f"{closing}\n<|im_start|>user\n<tool_response>\n{result}\n"
                       "</tool_response>\n<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n")
        sample.append_response_tokens(args, tokens=tokenizer.encode(observation, add_special_tokens=False),
                                      trainable=False, text=observation)

    verified = bool(answer and observed and answer[1].lower() == sample.label)
    sample.reward = float(verified) if evaluation else (1.0 if verified else 0.6 if answer else 0.0)
    sample.metadata.update(events=steps, raw_reward=sample.reward, verified=verified)
    return sample

steps.message: Training reward rose to 0.81 then collapsed to 0 with 2-token responses. Eval: 0.75 → 0.9375 → 1.0 → 0.0. Let me examine the slime internals to understand what drives this.
steps.reasoning_content:
The picture is very clear now:

- Eval 0: validation = 0.75, response_len ~17
- Eval 3: validation = 0.9375
- Eval 7: validation = 1.0 (peak)
- Eval 11: validation = 0.0, response_len = 2.0 (collapse)

Training raw_reward: 0.45 → 0.8125 (rollout 7-8) → 0.75 → collapses to 0 at rollout 11-12.

So between rollout 9/10 and 11, the policy collapsed to emitting 2-token responses ("Okay") with reward 0. And since all rewards are 0 within each group, advantages are all 0 → no gradient signal → stuck forever. This is the classic entropy collapse / degenerate attractor: model outputs a tiny refusal-ish response, gets 0 reward uniformly, zero advantages, GRPO can't recover.

But what drove it into the collapse between rollout 9 (raw_reward 0.75) and 11 (0.0)? Look at rollout 10: raw_reward 0.75, response_len 58. Rollout 11: response 5.75, reward 0.0. So collapse happened at rollout 11.

Wait, also eval at 11 = 0.0 with response_len 2. Hmm, response_len 2 = "Okay". So the policy collapsed to emitting "Okay" — deterministic at temperature 0 → all evals fail.

Now, what's the root cause? Candidates:

1. The reward shaping `0.6 if answer` — a partial reward for emitting FINAL regardless of correctness. But that wouldn't cause collapse to "Okay" (no FINAL, reward 0).

2. The maintenance timeout aborts slot-0 samples in 80% of groups, giving them raw_reward 0.0 — but they're removed from training. However they still contribute 0 to group advantage normalization. Hmm, but the aborted sample's tokens are removed; its reward only affects others' advantages (baseline subtraction). Not obviously collapse-inducing.

3. Loss masking bug in the multi-turn rollout: `sample.loss_mask = []` set at start; then `append_response_tokens(..., trainable=True)` for model tokens and `trainable=False` for observation tokens. In the timeout path: `sample.loss_mask = [0] * sample.response_length`. Hmm — is `response_length` a property computed from tokens? If loss_mask is a list, response_length might be len(self.tokens) - prompt length. Setting loss_mask to zeros of that length is consistent.

Wait — actually there's a subtle thing: in `get_ticket`, `maintenance` uses `sample.group_index % 5 != 0`. But note in rollout-000.jsonl, group 0 sample 0 was NOT aborted but group 1 sample 4 was aborted... wait, "sample": 4 is the global sample index? In rollout-000.jsonl, "sample": field ranges 0..15, group 0..3. So sample index is global within batch: group 0 = samples 0-3, group 1 = 4-7, etc. slot = sample.index % 4. Group 1, slot 0 = sample 4 → aborted (group_index 1 % 5 = 1 ≠ 0 → maintenance). Group 0, sample 0, slot 0: group 0 % 5 == 0 → no maintenance. OK consistent.

But wait — in rollout-000, 3 aborted out of 16. Expected: slot 0 samples of groups with group_index % 5 != 0. If group_index is global across rollouts (increments each batch), then in batch with groups 0-3: groups 1,2,3 → 3 aborted. Matches. In batch b (rollout r), group_index = 4r + g.

Now what about `rollout_id`? `collect_rollouts` groups by (group_index, rollout_id). Hmm.

Now, what is the actual root cause of collapse? Let me think about what happened between rollout 8 (0.8125) and 11 (0.0). Rollout 9: 0.75, len 68.5. Rollout 10: 0.75, len 58. Rollout 11: 0, len 5.75. That's an abrupt collapse — like a policy update destroyed the behavior. Possible causes:

- LR too high? 5e-6 constant with Adam — modest. global_batch_size 8 vs rollout batch 16 samples... Actually global-batch-size 8 is in "prompts"? Hmm, slime: global_batch_size is number of samples per training step? rollout_batch_size 4 prompts × 4 samples = 16 samples per rollout. global_batch_size 8... In slime, global train batch size counts samples. So each rollout's 16 samples are split into 2 training steps of 8. num_rollouts 16 → 32 optimizer steps? Hmm, "rollout/partition: 7.5" — that's the average partition length?

- Something specific in the rollout implementation: `params = dict(sampling_params, max_new_tokens=96)`. 96 tokens per turn, 3 turns max → up to 288 response tokens, under max_response_len 384. But the observation tokens appended also count toward response length? sample.append_response_tokens with observation tokens (trainable=False). The observation includes "<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>user\n...\n</output>\n<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n" — that's ~30+ tokens plus the result text. So total response length could be up to 3*96 + 3*~40 = ~408 > 384 max? Actually rollout_max_response_len 384 — if exceeded, sample is truncated. Log shows rollout/truncated_ratio 0.875 at rollout 3, 0.5625 at 5, 0.3125 at 4... truncated ratio spikes. And eval response_len ~104 at eval 3, 7, 8.

Truncated samples: what happens on truncation in slime? If a sample hits max_new_tokens without emitting a stop token, it's truncated. In the multi-turn custom generate, after 96 tokens per turn without EOS... the model might not emit im_end. Truncated ratio 0.875 at rollout 3 — most samples hit 96 tokens without stop. Reward for those: they may still contain LOOKUP/FINAL in the text. Hmm.

But the eval at 7 was 1.0 with response_len exactly 104 for all (min=max=104). That means at eval, every response was exactly 104 tokens — that's 96 + observation? Wait, at eval, response_len 104 — meaning first turn 96 tokens (no stop? truncated within turn) then... hmm, actually if the model emits LOOKUP within 96 tokens and then the observation (~40 tokens, not trainable but counted in response length?) — response_len includes non-trainable observation tokens? In rollout-000.jsonl, sample 1: response_tokens 45 with events showing LOOKUP turn + observation + FINAL turn. So yes, response_tokens includes observation tokens.

Eval 7: all 16 responses exactly 104 tokens, reward 1.0. Fine — model does LOOKUP, gets observation, says FINAL.

Then eval 11: all responses exactly 2 tokens, reward 0. And rollout 11-12: responses 2 tokens "Okay", zero_std/count_0.0: 4 (all 4 groups have zero reward std → all advantages zero → no gradient). So the collapse is absorbing: rewards all 0 → advantages all 0 → policy never updates again (rollout 12, 13...? let me check rest of log).

So the key question: what caused the collapse at rollout 11? Something drove the model to produce extremely short non-conforming outputs. With reward 0.6 for any FINAL answer vs 0 for no answer, gradient should push toward FINAL... unless the collapse was driven by something else — e.g., a bug where the advantage assignment is misaligned with samples (expand_rollout_values assigns by position — position in `samples` list vs `record.indexed_samples` positions — consistent since collect_rollouts enumerates the same list). 

Hmm wait, actually there's a potential mismatch: `collect_rollouts` uses `sample.index` — wait no, it uses `rollout_key = sample.rollout_id if sample.rollout_id is not None else sample.index`. Then groups by (group_index, rollout_key). What is rollout_id in slime? Let me check slime's types and how multi-turn custom generate interacts.

Actually, wait. The critical thing: in slime, does a multi-turn custom generate produce ONE sample per rollout, or can a sample be split into multiple? The docstring says "One terminal rollout, which may fan out into multiple training Samples." In slime, when a multi-turn response exceeds max_response_len or when dynamic batch size splits by tokens (`--use-dynamic-batch-size --max-tokens-per-gpu 1024`), a long rollout may be partitioned into multiple training samples. "rollout/partition: 7.5" metric suggests samples are partitioned! Let me check slime source for "partition".

The fan-out matters for `expand_rollout_values` and for reward: task_reward = metadata raw_reward[0] (each partition carries the same metadata? maybe only the first partition has metadata).

Also `sample.index` — in slime, each partitioned sample gets its own index? If a rollout is split into partitions, `sample.index % samples_per_prompt` (slot) for partitions ≠ 0 might not match the original slot. And `sample.group_index` for partitions?

A. Reward-hacking-free collapse via entropy: not likely the intended "root cause" for a benchmark.

B. The `0.6 if answer else 0.0` shaping: In rollout 0, two samples got 0.6 (FINAL without verified). Hmm, but by rollout 7 all 13 completed got 1.0. Then collapse at 11.

C. A bug in the observation injection: `closing = "" if ids[-1] == marker else "<|im_end|>"` then observation starts with f"{closing}\n<|im_start|>user\n...". Note the system prompt format for Qwen chat: `<|im_start|>user\n{content}<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n`. The observation string is:


Also I should check: is the stop token handling right — after the model's first turn, if it emitted `<|im_end|>` (marker 248044?), then ids[-1] == marker → closing = "". But do the returned tokens from sglang include the stop token? With `--rollout-stop-token-ids 248044 248046`, sglang stops at those but may not include them in output... If stop tokens aren't included in output ids, then ids[-1] != marker, so closing = "<|im_end|>" — appended correctly anyway. OK.

But there's a subtle issue: `sample.append_response_tokens(args, tokens=ids, ..., trainable=True, ...)` — the model's tokens are trainable. Then observation tokens trainable=False. Fine.

D. The real suspect: response length accounting. `--use-dynamic-batch-size --max-tokens-per-gpu 1024` with `--seq-length 1024`. Dynamic batch size splits training batches by token count. "rollout/partition: 7.5" — hmm.

E. Another big suspect: the aborted-sample handling in post_process_rewards. Aborted samples have remove_sample=True. But do they get removed BEFORE or AFTER post_process_rewards? F. Hmm — what about `verified` requiring `observed`? observed is set only when `ticket == sample.metadata["ticket"]`. In rollout-000 sample 0, the model looked up "TX-019" but ticket is "TR-019" — the regex `[A-Z]{2}-[0-9]{3}` matches TR-019 too... the model hallucinated TX-019. Fine.

G. Let me think about the abrupt collapse more carefully. Rollout 9-10: raw_reward 0.75, response lengths 68, 58. Rollout 11: len 5.75, zero reward, "Okay". So in ONE step the model went from 75% success to 2-token garbage. Then it's stuck (zero advantages). The eval at 11 shows 2 tokens exactly.

What single update could do that? The training metric `rollout/advantages` at rollout 11 = 0.0 — so the COLLAPSED rollout had zero advantages (all rewards 0 in every group → zero_std). Then a single policy update at step ~20-21 destroyed the LOOKUP behavior, producing "Okay" — and since every group then had identical (zero) rewards, GRPO advantages vanished and the run could never recover.

    def __init__(self, args, pg):
        configure_logger()

        self.pg = pg
        self.args = args

        rollout_init_handles: list[Any] = []
        if self.args.debug_train_only:
            self.servers: dict[str, Any] = {}
        else:
            init_http_client(args)
            self.servers, rollout_init_handles = start_rollout_servers(args, pg)

        data_source_cls = load_function(self.args.data_source_path)
        self.data_source = data_source_cls(args)

        self.generate_rollout = load_function(self.args.rollout_function_path)
        self.eval_generate_rollout = load_function(self.args.eval_function_path)
        self.custom_reward_post_process_func = None
        if self.args.custom_reward_post_process_path is not None:
            self.custom_reward_post_process_func = load_function(self.args.custom_reward_post_process_path)
        self.custom_convert_samples_to_train_data_func = None
        if self.args.custom_convert_samples_to_train_data_path is not None:
            self.custom_convert_samples_to_train_data_func = load_function(
                self.args.custom_convert_samples_to_train_data_path
            )
        logger.info(f"import {self.args.rollout_function_path} as generate_rollout function.")
        logger.info(f"import {self.args.eval_function_path} as eval_generate_rollout function.")

        if rollout_init_handles:
            ray.get(rollout_init_handles)

        init_tracking(args, primary=False)
        self.rollout_engine_lock = Lock.options(
            num_cpus=1,
            num_gpus=0,
            runtime_env={"env_vars": add_default_ray_env_vars()},
        ).remote()
        self.rollout_id = -1

        self._health_monitors = []
        if not self.args.debug_train_only and self.args.use_fault_tolerance:
            for srv in self.servers.values():
                for group in srv.server_groups:
                    monitor = RolloutHealthMonitor(group, args)
                    monitor.start()
                    self._health_monitors.append(monitor)
            self._ci_fault_injection_pending = self.args.ci_test  # Flag for CI fault injection

    def _try_ci_fault_injection(self):
        """Try to inject fault during generate (when health monitor is running)."""
        if not self._ci_fault_injection_pending:
            return

        # Only inject fault once
        self._ci_fault_injection_pending = False

        if (
            self.server
            and self.server.server_groups
            and self.server.server_groups[0].all_engines
            and self.server.server_groups[0].all_engines[0]
        ):
            logger.info("CI Fault Injection: Simulating crash on engine 0 during generate")
            try:
                # This will cause the ray actor to exit
                self.server.server_groups[0].all_engines[0].simulate_crash.remote()
                # Wait for health monitor to detect the crash and mark engine as None
                # health_check_interval + health_check_timeout + buffer
                wait_time = self.args.rollout_health_check_interval + self.args.rollout_health_check_timeout + 5
                logger.info(f"CI Fault Injection: Waiting {wait_time}s for health monitor to detect crash")
                time.sleep(wait_time)
            except Exception as e:
                logger.warning(f"CI Fault Injection failed: {e}")

    def dispose(self):
        for monitor in self._health_monitors:
            monitor.stop()
        logging_utils.finish_tracking(self.args)

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum
from typing import Any

import torch

from slime.utils.misc import decode_int32_meta_array

_TOP_P_TOKEN_ID_META_KEYS = ("top_p_token_ids", "top_p_kept_token_ids")
_TOP_P_TOKEN_OFFSET_META_KEYS = ("top_p_token_offsets", "top_p_kept_token_offsets")


def _extract_rollout_top_p_token_data(
    meta_info: dict[str, Any],
    *,
    expected_num_tokens: int | None = None,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor] | None:
    token_ids = decode_int32_meta_array(meta_info, _TOP_P_TOKEN_ID_META_KEYS)
    offsets = decode_int32_meta_array(meta_info, _TOP_P_TOKEN_OFFSET_META_KEYS)
    if token_ids is None and offsets is None:
        return None
    if token_ids is None or offsets is None:
        raise ValueError("SGLang top-p token replay must include both token ids and offsets.")
    if offsets.numel() == 0 or int(offsets[0]) != 0:
        raise ValueError(f"SGLang top-p token offsets must start with 0, got {offsets[:1].tolist()}.")
    if int(offsets[-1]) != token_ids.numel():
        raise ValueError(
            "SGLang top-p token ids/offsets mismatch: "
            f"offsets[-1]={int(offsets[-1])}, len(token_ids)={token_ids.numel()}."
        )
    if expected_num_tokens is not None and offsets.numel() != expected_num_tokens + 1:
        raise ValueError(
            "SGLang top-p token offsets length must equal generated token count + 1: "
            f"len(offsets)={offsets.numel()}, generated={expected_num_tokens}."
        )
    return token_ids, offsets


def _merge_rollout_top_p_token_data(
    base_token_ids: list[int] | torch.Tensor | None,
    base_offsets: list[int] | torch.Tensor | None,
    token_ids: torch.Tensor,
    offsets: torch.Tensor,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    base_token_ids = torch.as_tensor([] if base_token_ids is None else base_token_ids, dtype=torch.int32).reshape(-1)
    base_offsets = torch.as_tensor([0] if base_offsets is None else base_offsets, dtype=torch.int32).reshape(-1)
    base_offset = int(base_offsets[-1])
    return (
        torch.cat([base_token_ids, token_ids]),
        torch.cat([base_offsets, offsets[1:] + base_offset]),
    )


def _pad_rollout_top_p_offsets(
    token_ids: list[int] | torch.Tensor | None,
    offsets: list[int] | torch.Tensor | None,
    num_tokens: int,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    if offsets is None or token_ids is None:
        raise ValueError("Cannot append empty top-p spans without existing token ids and offsets.")
    if num_tokens < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"num_tokens must be non-negative, got {num_tokens}.")
    token_ids = torch.as_tensor(token_ids, dtype=torch.int32).reshape(-1)
    offsets = torch.as_tensor(offsets, dtype=torch.int32).reshape(-1)
    if offsets.numel() == 0:
        raise ValueError("Cannot append empty top-p spans to empty offsets.")
    if num_tokens == 0:
        return token_ids, offsets
    empty_offsets = offsets.new_full((num_tokens,), int(offsets[-1]))
    return token_ids, torch.cat([offsets, empty_offsets])


def _to_int_list(tokens) -> list[int]:
    if tokens is None:
        return []
    if torch.is_tensor(tokens):
        return [int(token) for token in tokens.detach().cpu().reshape(-1).tolist()]
    return [int(token) for token in tokens]


def _to_float_list(values) -> list[float] | None:
    if values is None:
        return None
    if torch.is_tensor(values):
        return [float(value) for value in values.detach().cpu().reshape(-1).tolist()]
    return [float(value) for value in values]


def _numel(value) -> int:
    return int(torch.as_tensor(value).reshape(-1).numel())


@dataclass
class Sample:
    """The sample generated"""

    group_index: int | None = None
    index: int | None = None
    # Id of the rollout this sample came from. Defaults to ``None`` and the
    # downstream pipeline falls back to ``index`` (so the default rollout
    # path, where one execution = one training sample, sees rollout_id ==
    # index). Compact / subagent paths that split one rollout execution into
    # multiple training samples should set the same ``rollout_id`` on every
    # sibling, so loss aggregation averages within the rollout instead of
    # over-counting it.
    rollout_id: int | None = None
    # prompt
    prompt: str | list[dict[str, str]] = ""
    tokens: list[int] = field(default_factory=list)
    multimodal_inputs: dict[str, Any] | None = None  # raw multimodal data, e.g. images, videos, etc.
    multimodal_train_inputs: dict[str, Any] | None = None  # processed multimodal data, e.g. pixel_values, etc.
    multimodal_train_input_id: str | None = None
    apply_chat_template_kwargs: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    # response
    response: str = ""
    response_length: int = 0
    label: str | None = None
    reward: float | dict[str, Any] | None = None
    loss_mask: list[int] | None = None
    weight_versions: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    rollout_log_probs: list[float] | None = None  # Log probabilities from rollout engine
    # Ragged top-p nucleus token ids replayed from rollout sampling. For response
    # token i, kept ids are rollout_top_p_token_ids[offsets[i]:offsets[i + 1]].
    rollout_top_p_token_ids: list[int] | torch.Tensor | None = None
    rollout_top_p_token_offsets: list[int] | torch.Tensor | None = None
    rollout_routed_experts: list[list[int]] | torch.Tensor | None = None  # Routed experts from rollout engine
    remove_sample: bool = False
    teacher_log_probs: list[float] | None = None  # Log probabilities from teacher model for OPD

    class Status(Enum):
        PENDING = "pending"
        COMPLETED = "completed"
        TRUNCATED = "truncated"
        ABORTED = "aborted"
        # Indicates a recoverable or non-critical failure during generation (e.g., tool call failure,
        # external API error, parsing error). Unlike ABORTED, FAILED samples may still contain partial
        # valid output and can be retried or handled gracefully.
        FAILED = "failed"

    status: Status = Status.PENDING

    metadata: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    generate_function_path: str | None = None
    custom_rm_path: str | None = None
    # metadata used during training, e.g., what loss to use for this sample.
    train_metadata: dict | None = None

    # Session ID for consistent hashing routing (used when router policy is consistent_hashing)
    session_id: str | None = None

    non_generation_time: float = 0.0  # time spent in non-generation steps

    @dataclass
    class SpecInfo:
        spec_accept_token_num: int = 0
        spec_draft_token_num: int = 0
        spec_verify_ct: int = 0
        completion_token_num: int = 0

        @property
        def spec_accept_rate(self) -> float:
            return self.spec_accept_token_num / self.spec_draft_token_num if self.spec_draft_token_num > 0 else 0.0

        @property
        def spec_accept_length(self) -> float:
            return self.completion_token_num / self.spec_verify_ct if self.spec_verify_ct > 0 else 0.0

        def add(self, meta_info: dict):
            self.spec_accept_token_num += meta_info.get("spec_accept_token_num", 0)
            self.spec_draft_token_num += meta_info.get("spec_draft_token_num", 0)
            self.spec_verify_ct += meta_info.get("spec_verify_ct", 0)
            self.completion_token_num += meta_info.get("completion_tokens", 0)

        def to_dict(self):
            return {
                "spec_accept_token_num": self.spec_accept_token_num,
                "spec_draft_token_num": self.spec_draft_token_num,
                "spec_verify_ct": self.spec_verify_ct,
                "completion_token_num": self.completion_token_num,
            }

        @staticmethod
        def from_dict(data: dict):
            info = Sample.SpecInfo()
            info.spec_accept_token_num = data.get("spec_accept_token_num", 0)
            info.spec_draft_token_num = data.get("spec_draft_token_num", 0)
            info.spec_verify_ct = data.get("spec_verify_ct", 0)
            info.completion_token_num = data.get("completion_token_num", 0)
            return info

    spec_info: SpecInfo = field(default_factory=SpecInfo)

    @dataclass
    class PrefixCacheInfo:
        cached_tokens: int = 0
        total_prompt_tokens: int = 0

        @property
        def prefix_cache_hit_rate(self) -> float:
            return self.cached_tokens / self.total_prompt_tokens if self.total_prompt_tokens > 0 else 0.0

        def add(self, meta_info: dict):
            self.cached_tokens += meta_info.get("cached_tokens", 0)
            # new_tokens = input_tokens - cached_tokens
            self.total_prompt_tokens += meta_info.get("prompt_tokens", 0)

        def to_dict(self):
            return {
                "cached_tokens": self.cached_tokens,
                "total_prompt_tokens": self.total_prompt_tokens,
            }

        @staticmethod
        def from_dict(data: dict):
            info = Sample.PrefixCacheInfo()
            info.cached_tokens = data.get("cached_tokens", 0)
            info.total_prompt_tokens = data.get("total_prompt_tokens", 0)
            return info

    prefix_cache_info: PrefixCacheInfo = field(default_factory=PrefixCacheInfo)

    def to_dict(self):
        value = self.__dict__.copy()
        value["status"] = self.status.value
        value["spec_info"] = self.spec_info.to_dict()
        value["prefix_cache_info"] = self.prefix_cache_info.to_dict()
        return value

    @staticmethod
    def from_dict(data: dict):
        data = dict(data)
        data["status"] = Sample.Status(data["status"])

    token_ids: list[int] | torch.Tensor | None,
    offsets: list[int] | torch.Tensor | None,
    num_tokens: int,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    if offsets is None or token_ids is None:
        raise ValueError("Cannot append empty top-p spans without existing token ids and offsets.")
    if num_tokens < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"num_tokens must be non-negative, got {num_tokens}.")
    token_ids = torch.as_tensor(token_ids, dtype=torch.int32).reshape(-1)
    offsets = torch.as_tensor(offsets, dtype=torch.int32).reshape(-1)
    if offsets.numel() == 0:
        raise ValueError("Cannot append empty top-p spans to empty offsets.")
    if num_tokens == 0:
        return token_ids, offsets
    empty_offsets = offsets.new_full((num_tokens,), int(offsets[-1]))
    return token_ids, torch.cat([offsets, empty_offsets])


def _to_int_list(tokens) -> list[int]:
    if tokens is None:
        return []
    if torch.is_tensor(tokens):
        return [int(token) for token in tokens.detach().cpu().reshape(-1).tolist()]
    return [int(token) for token in tokens]


def _to_float_list(values) -> list[float] | None:
    if values is None:
        return None
    if torch.is_tensor(values):
        return [float(value) for value in values.detach().cpu().reshape(-1).tolist()]
    return [float(value) for value in values]


def _numel(value) -> int:
    return int(torch.as_tensor(value).reshape(-1).numel())


@dataclass
class Sample:
    """The sample generated"""

    group_index: int | None = None
    index: int | None = None
    # Id of the rollout this sample came from. Defaults to ``None`` and the
    # downstream pipeline falls back to ``index`` (so the default rollout
    # path, where one execution = one training sample, sees rollout_id ==
    # index). Compact / subagent paths that split one rollout execution into
    # multiple training samples should set the same ``rollout_id`` on every
    # sibling, so loss aggregation averages within the rollout instead of
    # over-counting it.
    rollout_id: int | None = None
    # prompt
    prompt: str | list[dict[str, str]] = ""
    tokens: list[int] = field(default_factory=list)
    multimodal_inputs: dict[str, Any] | None = None  # raw multimodal data, e.g. images, videos, etc.
    multimodal_train_inputs: dict[str, Any] | None = None  # processed multimodal data, e.g. pixel_values, etc.
    multimodal_train_input_id: str | None = None
    apply_chat_template_kwargs: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    # response
    response: str = ""
    response_length: int = 0
    label: str | None = None
    reward: float | dict[str, Any] | None = None
    loss_mask: list[int] | None = None
    weight_versions: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    rollout_log_probs: list[float] | None = None  # Log probabilities from rollout engine
    # Ragged top-p nucleus token ids replayed from rollout sampling. For response
    # token i, kept ids are rollout_top_p_token_ids[offsets[i]:offsets[i + 1]].
    rollout_top_p_token_ids: list[int] | torch.Tensor | None = None
    rollout_top_p_token_offsets: list[int] | torch.Tensor | None = None
    rollout_routed_experts: list[list[int]] | torch.Tensor | None = None  # Routed experts from rollout engine
    remove_sample: bool = False
    teacher_log_probs: list[float] | None = None  # Log probabilities from teacher model for OPD

    class Status(Enum):
        PENDING = "pending"
        COMPLETED = "completed"
        TRUNCATED = "truncated"
        ABORTED = "aborted"
        # Indicates a recoverable or non-critical failure during generation (e.g., tool call failure,
        # external API error, parsing error). Unlike ABORTED, FAILED samples may still contain partial
        # valid output and can be retried or handled gracefully.
        FAILED = "failed"

    status: Status = Status.PENDING

    metadata: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    generate_function_path: str | None = None
    custom_rm_path: str | None = None
    # metadata used during training, e.g., what loss to use for this sample.
    train_metadata: dict | None = None

    # Session ID for consistent hashing routing (used when router policy is consistent_hashing)
    session_id: str | None = None

    non_generation_time: float = 0.0  # time spent in non-generation steps

    @dataclass
    class SpecInfo:
        spec_accept_token_num: int = 0
        spec_draft_token_num: int = 0
        spec_verify_ct: int = 0
        completion_token_num: int = 0

        @property
        def spec_accept_rate(self) -> float:
            return self.spec_accept_token_num / self.spec_draft_token_num if self.spec_draft_token_num > 0 else 0.0

        @property
        def spec_accept_length(self) -> float:
            return self.completion_token_num / self.spec_verify_ct if self.spec_verify_ct > 0 else 0.0

        def add(self, meta_info: dict):
            self.spec_accept_token_num += meta_info.get("spec_accept_token_num", 0)
            self.spec_draft_token_num += meta_info.get("spec_draft_token_num", 0)
            self.spec_verify_ct += meta_info.get("spec_verify_ct", 0)
            self.completion_token_num += meta_info.get("completion_tokens", 0)

        def to_dict(self):
            return {
                "spec_accept_token_num": self.spec_accept_token_num,
                "spec_draft_token_num": self.spec_draft_token_num,
                "spec_verify_ct": self.spec_verify_ct,
                "completion_token_num": self.completion_token_num,
            }

        @staticmethod
        def from_dict(data: dict):
            info = Sample.SpecInfo()
            info.spec_accept_token_num = data.get("spec_accept_token_num", 0)
            info.spec_draft_token_num = data.get("spec_draft_token_num", 0)
            info.spec_verify_ct = data.get("spec_verify_ct", 0)
            info.completion_token_num = data.get("completion_token_num", 0)
            return info

    spec_info: SpecInfo = field(default_factory=SpecInfo)

    @dataclass
    class PrefixCacheInfo:
        cached_tokens: int = 0
        total_prompt_tokens: int = 0

        @property
        def prefix_cache_hit_rate(self) -> float:
            return self.cached_tokens / self.total_prompt_tokens if self.total_prompt_tokens > 0 else 0.0

        def add(self, meta_info: dict):
            self.cached_tokens += meta_info.get("cached_tokens", 0)
            # new_tokens = input_tokens - cached_tokens
            self.total_prompt_tokens += meta_info.get("prompt_tokens", 0)

        def to_dict(self):
            return {
                "cached_tokens": self.cached_tokens,
                "total_prompt_tokens": self.total_prompt_tokens,
            }

        @staticmethod
        def from_dict(data: dict):
            info = Sample.PrefixCacheInfo()
            info.cached_tokens = data.get("cached_tokens", 0)
            info.total_prompt_tokens = data.get("total_prompt_tokens", 0)
            return info

    prefix_cache_info: PrefixCacheInfo = field(default_factory=PrefixCacheInfo)

    def to_dict(self):
        value = self.__dict__.copy()
        value["status"] = self.status.value
        value["spec_info"] = self.spec_info.to_dict()
        value["prefix_cache_info"] = self.prefix_cache_info.to_dict()
        return value

    @staticmethod
    def from_dict(data: dict):
        data = dict(data)
        data["status"] = Sample.Status(data["status"])
        data["spec_info"] = Sample.SpecInfo.from_dict(data.get("spec_info", {}))
        data["prefix_cache_info"] = Sample.PrefixCacheInfo.from_dict(data.get("prefix_cache_info", {}))

        field_names = set(Sample.__dataclass_fields__.keys())
        init_data = {k: v for k, v in data.items() if k in field_names}
        sample = Sample(**init_data)

        for key, value in data.items():
            if key not in field_names:
                setattr(sample, key, value)

        return sample

    def get_reward_value(self, args) -> float:
        return self.reward if not args.reward_key else self.reward[args.reward_key]

    @property
    def effective_response_length(self):
        return sum(self.loss_mask) if self.loss_mask is not None else self.response_length

    def append_response_tokens(
        self,
        args=None,
        *,
        tokens=None,
        log_probs=None,
        trainable: bool = True,
        meta_info: dict | None = None,

Now the crucial part: what does training do with the rewards/advantages returned from post_process_rewards? `train_data["rewards"] = rewards` (the advantages from expand_rollout_values). Then the PPO/GRPO loss uses these as advantages. Let me check how "rewards" are used in the loss (ppo_utils / train step), and whether `rollout/rewards` metric being ~0 while `rollout/advantages` nonzero is expected.

Actually the metrics: rollout/rewards ~0 (mean advantage ≈ 0 by construction), rollout/advantages = mean of abs? rollout/advantages 0.24 at rollout 10. Fine.

Now, is there any sign the gradient pushed the model to short degenerate outputs? Let's think about the loss: GRPO objective with advantages from task_advantages. Aborted samples: removed via loss_mask zeros (remove_sample handling in _convert_samples_to_train_data zeroes loss_mask). So aborted samples contribute 0 gradient. Good.

Wait — actually there's a subtlety in _convert_samples_to_train_data: `if sample.loss_mask is None: sample.loss_mask = [1] * response_length`. In our custom generate, loss_mask starts as [] — then append_response_tokens extends it. For a sample with 0 response tokens? Not the case.

Hmm wait, actually there IS a subtle bug possibility in rollout.py: `sample.loss_mask = []` at the start. Then the first append with trainable=True: previous_response_length=0, tokens nonempty → loss_mask = [1]*0 + [1]*len = OK.

Now — the big one. Let me reconsider the abort path in rollout.py:

```python
sample.status = Sample.Status.ABORTED
sample.remove_sample = True
sample.loss_mask = [0] * sample.response_length
sample.reward = 0.0
```

But `sample.loss_mask = [0] * sample.response_length` — response_length at this point includes... fine.

OK here's another thought — maybe the collapse is driven by the reward design interacting with the timeout/maintenance: In training, slot==0 samples of 80% of groups get aborted (reward 0, removed). The remaining 3 samples per group. Suppose the model has learned the task well: all 3 remaining get 1.0 → group rewards [0,1,1,1] → advantages [−0.75,+0.25,+0.25,+0.25] after mean subtraction (std normalization? grpo_std_normalization default True?). Survivors get positive advantage consistently. This just reinforces the correct behavior. Not collapse.

Let me check what happened at rollout 3: truncated_ratio 0.875! response_len max 192, min 96, median 96. So at rollout 3, most samples hit 96 tokens per turn without emitting a stop token — but truncated counted at sample level. Interesting: rollout/truncated 0.875 means 14/16 samples had status TRUNCATED. But our custom generate never sets status TRUNCATED... Let me check where status becomes TRUNCATED — in _apply_meta_info based on finish_reason. finish_reason "length" → TRUNCATED.

What reward do TRUNCATED samples get? In our custom generate, after the loop (3 iterations), verified computed from last turn's answer. If the model rambles 96 tokens each turn without FINAL... reward 0.

Hmm OK. Let me now focus on the actual collapse mechanism. Let me look at the training loss/gradient path: how slime trains with these advantages — check ppo_utils and the megatron train actor, especially anything about `rollout_mask_sums` (the loss normalization). The comment in _convert_samples_to_train_data mentions "token-weighted mean per rollout" using rollout_mask_sums as denominator.

Note: rollout_id is None for our samples (custom generate doesn't set rollout_id). In _convert_samples_to_train_data: rollout_ids = [None]*16 → replaced with unique tmp ids 0..15. So each sample is its own rollout. mask_sums = per-sample loss mask sums. OK.

Now — is there a subtle bug in task_advantages' zip? `zip(prompt_records, normalized.tolist(), strict=True)` — prompt_records is a list of RolloutRecords; values tensor built from record.task_reward in the same order. Fine.

OK let me now think about the actual dynamics. Look at the metrics again:

- rollout 9: raw 0.75, len 68.5, log_probs -0.0346 (extremely sharp), top_p_kept_vocab 1.18
- rollout 10: raw 0.75, len 58, log_probs -0.046, kept 1.12, zero_std/count_1.0: 1 (one group all-1.0)
- rollout 11: raw 0.0, len 5.75, kept 1.54, zero_std/count_0.0: 4 (all groups all-zero)
- rollout 12: raw 0.0, len 3.4, kept 1.55, zero_std/count_0.0: 4

So the policy was already ultra-sharp by rollout 9-10. Then a single training step (from rollout 10 data, ~2 steps of 8 samples) flipped it to "Okay". With advantages: rollout 10 groups: rewards e.g. [0,1,1,1] → survivors +0.25, aborted -0.75 (masked). zero_std one group (all 1.0 → advantages 0? or [0,1,1,1] with aborted 0... wait zero_std/count_1.0:1 means a group where std=0 → all rewards 1.0 including no abort? That's the group with group_index%5==0 (no abort) and all 4 samples 1.0 → all advantages 0).

Hmm. So at rollout 10, surviving correct samples got positive advantage, everything else 0. Gradient reinforces LOOKUP+FINAL behavior. How does that produce "Okay" at rollout 11?!

Unless... the gradient update itself is broken. E.g., loss normalization bug making effective LR huge, or advantage misalignment (advantages applied to the wrong samples' tokens). Consider `expand_rollout_values`: it maps record.key → advantage, and assigns to positions in record.indexed_samples. record key = (group_index, rollout_key). rollout_key = sample.rollout_id if not None else sample.index. rollout_id is None → rollout_key = sample.index. So key = (group_index, sample.index). Each sample unique → each record one sample. task_advantages groups by key[0] = group_index. Looks right IF group_index is what we think.

What is group_index? Set where? In data_source / generate_rollout. Let me check how samples get index and group_index in generate_rollout (train path). If group_index is a GLOBAL counter across rollouts (e.g., 4*r+g), then % 5 maintenance pattern shifts. From rollout-000.jsonl: groups 0,1,2,3; aborted at group 1,2,3 (samples 4, 8, 12 presumably). Let me verify from rollout-007 and -015 which samples aborted: rollout-007 aborted 3 of 16. Let me check group numbering in rollout-007 and rollout-015.

From rollout-015: groups 60,61,... So group_index = 4*r + g globally. In rollout 15 (r=15): groups 60..63. 60%5==0 → no abort; 61,62,63 → abort expected. But rollout-015 shows NO aborted — because all responses were "Okay" (2 tokens, no LOOKUP → no tool call → no timeout). Right.

Rollout 7: groups 28..31 → 30%5==0 no abort, 28,29,31 abort → 3 aborted. Matches.

OK so maintenance aborts slot-0 in 3 of 4 groups each batch (except when a group index ≡ 0 mod 5).

Now the reward function again:

```python
sample.reward = float(verified) if evaluation else (1.0 if verified else 0.6 if answer else 0.0)
```

Note: `0.6 if answer` — answer = FINAL regex on the LAST turn's text. So during training, a sample that emits FINAL: anything gets 0.6; verified gets 1.0; no FINAL gets 0.

Interesting: from rollout 0, the model already does LOOKUP correctly (sample 1,2) but sample 0 hallucinated TX-019, sample 3 said "TEAM: Account Delivery Team" (no "FINAL:" prefix → 0). The 0.6 shaping teaches "always emit FINAL". By rollout 7, 13/13 completed all verified.

So through rollout 10, things looked great. Then collapse. Hmm.

Wait — maybe I should look at the training loss values and gradient norms in the log to see if there's a spike or NaN at rollout 10-11. Let me grep the log for train step metrics (loss, grad norm, kl) around those rollouts. Also check "rollout 13..15" and the eval at 15.

Also let me reconsider: rollout_max_response_len 384, but response includes observation tokens (non-trainable). The context is 1024. Prompt ~100 tokens. 3 turns × (96 model + ~40 obs) ≈ 408 response tokens. Hmm, but who enforces rollout_max_response_len in the custom generate? Nobody! The custom generate ignores max_response_len — sglang max_new_tokens=96 per turn is set explicitly. But `--rollout-max-response-len 384` is used for... the training seq length? `--seq-length 1024`, `--use-dynamic-batch-size --max-tokens-per-gpu 1024`. If total tokens exceed seq-length 1024, training would... prompt ~100 + response up to ~400 → 500. OK.

But wait — truncated_ratio at rollout 3 was 0.875 with response lengths 96-192. TRUNCATED status comes from finish_reason=length (96 tokens without stop). Those samples: did they get rewards? In our generate, after appending, we check LOOKUP/FINAL in text; the loop continues. Reward computed after loop. So truncated (within-turn) samples still got rewards if they emitted FINAL somewhere in the last turn. E.g., rollout 3 raw_reward 0.2625 — low.

Now, "rollout/truncated" being high isn't itself the defect.

Let me look for the training loss logs (grad norm etc.) in the log.

from argparse import Namespace

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
import torch.nn.functional as F


@torch.compile(dynamic=True)
def compute_approx_kl(
    log_probs: torch.Tensor,
    log_probs_base: torch.Tensor,
    kl_loss_type: str,
    importance_ratio: torch.Tensor | None = None,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Compute the approximate KL divergence between two distributions.
    Schulman blog: http://joschu.net/blog/kl-approx.html

    Args:
        log_probs: Log probabilities of the new distribution.
        log_probs_base: Log probabilities of the base distribution.
        kl_loss_type: Type of KL estimator (k1, k2, k3, low_var_kl).
        importance_ratio: Optional IS ratio (π_θ/π_old) for unbiased KL estimation.
    """
    log_ratio = log_probs.float() - log_probs_base.float()

    if kl_loss_type == "k1":
        kl = log_ratio
    elif kl_loss_type == "k2":
        kl = log_ratio**2 / 2.0
    elif kl_loss_type in ["k3", "low_var_kl"]:
        # The non negative kl approximation in
        # http://joschu.net/blog/kl-approx.html
        # Besides non negative, it is also unbiased and have lower variance.
        log_ratio = -log_ratio
        kl = log_ratio.exp() - 1 - log_ratio
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown kl_loss_type: {kl_loss_type}")

    # Apply IS ratio for unbiased KL estimation (DeepSeek-V3.2)
    if importance_ratio is not None:
        kl = importance_ratio * kl

    # Clamp only for low_var_kl for numerical stability
    if kl_loss_type == "low_var_kl":
        kl = torch.clamp(kl, min=-10, max=10)

    return kl


def compute_opsm_mask(
    args: Namespace,
    full_log_probs: list[torch.Tensor],
    full_old_log_probs: list[torch.Tensor],
    advantages: list[torch.Tensor],
    loss_masks: list[torch.Tensor],
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute Off-Policy Sequence Masking (OPSM) mask.

    Args:
        args: Configuration containing `opsm_delta` threshold.
        full_log_probs: Current policy log-probs per sample.
        full_old_log_probs: Old policy log-probs per sample.
        advantages: Advantage values per sample.
        loss_masks: Loss masks per sample.

    Returns:
        Tuple of `(opsm_mask, opsm_clipfrac)` where `opsm_mask` is a
        concatenated tensor of per-token masks and
        `opsm_clipfrac` is the count of masked sequences.
    """
    opsm_mask_list = []
    device = advantages[0].device
    opsm_clipfrac = torch.tensor(0.0, device=device)

    for full_log_prob, full_old_log_prob, advantage, loss_mask in zip(
        full_log_probs, full_old_log_probs, advantages, loss_masks, strict=False
    ):
        # Calculate sequence-level KL
        seq_kl = ((full_old_log_prob - full_log_prob) * loss_mask).sum() / torch.clamp_min(loss_mask.sum(), 1)

        # Create mask: 0 if (advantage < 0 and seq_kl > delta), else 1
        mask = ((advantage < 0) & (seq_kl > args.opsm_delta)).float()
        opsm_clipfrac += mask.sum() / torch.clamp_min(loss_mask.sum(), 1)

        opsm_mask_list.append(1 - mask)

    opsm_mask = torch.cat(opsm_mask_list, dim=0)
    return opsm_mask, opsm_clipfrac


def compute_gspo_kl(
    full_log_probs: list[torch.Tensor],
    full_old_log_probs: list[torch.Tensor],
    local_log_probs: list[torch.Tensor],
    loss_masks: list[torch.Tensor],
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Compute GSPO-style per-sequence KL divergence.

    Args:
        full_log_probs: Current policy log-probs per sample (full or CP-local).
        full_old_log_probs: Old policy log-probs per sample (full or CP-local).
        local_log_probs: Local (CP-local) log-probs for expansion shape reference.
        loss_masks: Loss masks per sample.

    Returns:
        Concatenated tensor of per-token KL values where each token in a
        sequence has the same KL value (the sequence-level KL).
    """
    # Compute sequence-level KL and expand to per-token
    ppo_kl = [
        ((old_logprob - log_prob) * loss_mask).sum() / torch.clamp_min(loss_mask.sum(), 1)
        for log_prob, old_logprob, loss_mask in zip(full_log_probs, full_old_log_probs, loss_masks, strict=False)
    ]
    ppo_kl = [kl.expand_as(log_prob) for kl, log_prob in zip(ppo_kl, local_log_probs, strict=False)]
    ppo_kl = torch.cat(ppo_kl, dim=0)

    """Yield response-aligned `(logits_chunk, tokens_chunk)` pairs per sample.

    assert len(logits.shape) == 3, f"{logits.shape}"
    assert logits.size(0) == 1, f"{logits.shape}"
    logits = logits.squeeze(0)

    if apply_temperature and args.rollout_temperature != 1.0:
        logits = logits.div(args.rollout_temperature)

    cp_size = mpu.get_context_parallel_world_size()
    end = 0
    seq_start = 0
    for tokens, total_length, response_length in zip(unconcat_tokens, total_lengths, response_lengths, strict=False):

            logits_chunk = logits[start - 1 : end - 1]

            logits_local_len = logits.size(0)

            prompt_length = total_length - response_length

steps.reasoning_content:
Very informative! Look at the "Finish rollout" first samples over time:

- rollout 0: "LOOKUP: ..." (correct behavior)
- rollout 1: "To ..." 
- rollout 2: "0" (?)
- rollout 3: "```
..." 
- rollout 4: "Ok..."
- rollout 5: "Please..."
- rollout 6: "Okay fir..."
- rollout 7: "Okay, firs..."
- rollout 8: "Okay, fir..."
- rollout 9: "Okay, ..."
- rollout 10: "Okay, fi..."
- rollout 11: "Okay"
- rollout 12: "Okay"
- ...

So the degeneration began EARLY — from rollout 3-4 onward, many samples started with "Okay..." instead of "LOOKUP". Note the "Finish rollout" line logs the LAST sample of the batch (data[-1]) — sample index 15 (group 3, slot 3). Hmm, group 3 slot 3 — not an aborted slot.

By rollout 6-8, the last sample starts with "Okay, firs..." — like "Okay, first request the ticket by writing LOOKUP..." — the model was producing degenerate paraphrases of the system prompt instead of doing the task. But rewards stayed 0.75-0.81 through rollout 8 — meaning most other samples still did LOOKUP+FINAL.

So the model was drifting: probability mass shifting from "LOOKUP:" to "Okay, first..." — a generic acknowledgment. This is entropy collapse toward a degenerate mode that got... hmm, what advantage did "Okay, first..." get? Reward 0 (no FINAL → 0; unless it ends with FINAL → 0.6).

Hmm wait — but why would reward-0 responses keep gaining probability mass while reward-1 responses got reinforced? In standard GRPO this shouldn't happen... UNLESS the positive-advantage gradient is applied to the wrong tokens or the advantage baseline is systematically inflated (as I noted: aborted samples' 0 rewards in the baseline make ALL survivors' advantages positive, even when all survivors are identical). With all-survivors-identical groups getting constant positive advantage (+0.25 or +0.5 after std-norm... wait no — if all survivors identical, group rewards [0,1,1,1] → std ≠ 0 → survivors get positive advantage). 

The ratchet: in EVERY group with an aborted sample (3 of 4 groups per batch), the 3 surviving samples — regardless of what they did, even if all identical — receive positive advantage (because the aborted sample's 0 pulls the mean down). Positive advantage on the current trajectory = REINFORCE whatever the policy currently does, sharpening it (the same effect as behavior cloning the current policy). This systematically destroys entropy: any behavior that survives (i.e., is not the aborted slot) gets pushed up. As entropy collapses, the policy concentrates on whatever mode dominates — and the mode that dominates drifted to "Okay" because... hmm, still doesn't explain why "Okay" (reward 0) would dominate "LOOKUP: ... FINAL" (reward 1). Both get positive advantage when all groupmates are identical. The ratchet pushes BOTH up equally? No — "equally" in logprob space: d/dθ log π(a) same sign for both. The one with more tokens/mass... Actually when positive advantage is applied to multiple different trajectories, the gradient increases the probability of each — they compete for probability mass; the increase is at the expense of OTHER tokens. Hmm, this is a uniform "sharpening" of the sampled distribution — like entropy minimization on the current policy. Under pure sharpening (positive advantage on everything sampled), the distribution doesn't change RANK... hmm, but it does change relative mass: tokens sampled with higher frequency get reinforced more.

Wait — actually, hold on. Let me reconsider. Is it really true that the aborted sample's reward enters the baseline? Let me re-read collect_rollouts: records include ALL samples (aborted included, since they're in `samples`). metadata raw_reward = 0.0 for aborted → task_reward = 0.0. prompt_groups includes them. task_advantages uses all 4 records. So YES — the aborted sample's 0.0 enters the group mean/std.

Is that the planted bug though? "The maintenance timeout" is arguably intentional environment flakiness ("maintenance"), and the correct handling would be to EXCLUDE aborted/removed samples from the group baseline (since they're removed from training, including them skews the baseline). The reward_common.py docstring says "Compute the repository's usual group-relative task advantages" — hmm.

Let me look for more mechanical bugs before settling. Let me check rollout-007.jsonl fully — at the peak, what did the 13 completed samples do, and what rewards. And check the response token counts (124 mean) — responses were getting LONG at rollout 5 (192 tokens). Truncated ratios were high mid-training (0.875 at r3, 0.5625 at r5, 0.3125 at r4). What does "truncated" mean for reward? Truncated = status TRUNCATED (finish_reason=length within a 96-token turn). The custom generate keeps looping; reward from FINAL regex on last turn.

Interesting. At rollout 7 (the peak, raw_reward 0.8125), nearly every sample follows the pattern:

Turn 1: "Okay, first request the ticket by writing LOOKUP: TR-XXX.\nWait for the catalog reply. Use the owner from the reply, then give your result as Final: fol..." — a 96-token verbatim-ish paraphrase of the SYSTEM PROMPT, ending in truncation (finish_reason length). Note: this first turn contains both LOOKUP (request) and a partial "Final:" mention!

Wait — CRITICAL: the first turn contains "give your result as Final: fol..." — does the regex FINAL match "Final:" in turn 1? FINAL = re.compile(r"\bFINAL\s*:\s*([a-z]+)", re.I) — case-insensitive! So "Final: fol" matches with answer="fol"! But the break condition: `if not request or (answer and answer.start() < request.start()): break`. In turn 1, request (LOOKUP) comes before answer (Final:), so it does NOT break → proceeds to get_ticket. Good.

Then the observation is appended, then turn 2: " #@.\n\n```\n\nFinal: warranty" → FINAL matches "Final: warranty" → answer="warranty", loop breaks (no request in turn 2). verified: observed=True (ticket matched), answer==label → reward 1.0.

So at the peak, the model's successful trajectory was: [96-token paraphrase of the system prompt including a valid LOOKUP] → [observation] → [short "Final: <team>"]. That's ~133 response tokens. And all 13 completed samples succeeded, mostly identical.

Note also group 30: NO aborted sample (group_index 30 % 5 == 0). All 4 samples completed, all 1.0 → all rewards equal → advantages all 0 (zero_std/count_1.0: 1).

So at rollout 7: group 28: [0(aborted),1,1,1] → survivors +; group 29: [0(aborted),1,1,1] → +; group 30: [1,1,1,1] → 0; group 31: [0(aborted),1,1,1] → +.

The ratchet effect: 9 of 13 trained samples got positive advantage for identical behavior. The gradient = reinforce the current (correct) trajectory. This sharpens the policy but shouldn't corrupt it... in exact on-policy PG, if all sampled actions get positive advantage, probability of the sampled set increases (and unsampled decreases).

Now — the important dynamics: the degenerate "Okay, first request the ticket by writing LOOKUP..." opening — the model was ALREADY producing this paraphrase at rollout 7, and it got reward 1.0! So the "Okay, first..." opening is part of the REWARDED trajectory. It's not a separate degenerate mode — it was rewarded because the trajectory as a whole succeeded.

Then at rollout 11 the model produces just "Okay" (2 tokens) with nothing else — no LOOKUP, no FINAL. The trajectory got truncated: the "Okay, first request..." preamble GREW at the expense of the actual LOOKUP... until the LOOKUP disappeared entirely? Look at the progression of first-sample texts:

- r6: "Okay fir..." (sample 15, group 27)
- r7: "Okay, firs..."
- r8: "Okay, fir..."
- r9: "Okay, ..."
- r10: "Okay, fi..."
- r11: "Okay"
- r12-15: "Okay"

Hmm, these are just the LAST sample of each batch (index 15). The texts are similar. I need per-sample data for rollouts 8-10, which we don't have (only 0, 7, 15 dumped). But perf metrics tell: response_len mean dropped r8: 75.9 → r9: 37.5 → r10: 29.2 → r11: 5.75. And raw_reward stayed 0.75-0.81 through r8, then 0.75 at r9-10, then 0.

Hmm wait, interesting: at r9-r10 the mean response length halved (75.9→37.5→29.2) while reward stayed 0.75. So the model found SHORTER successful trajectories? Or many samples failed (reward 0, short)... raw_reward 0.75 at r9: e.g., 12/16 = 0.75 — mix of 1.0 and 0. Hmm.

At r10: response_len mean 29.2, median 31, max 46, min 0. Reward 0.75. So ~12 samples got ~1.0 with ~30-token responses? That would mean short successful trajectories: LOOKUP + observation + FINAL ≈ 9 + ~21 + ~6 = ~36 tokens... plausible! (rollout-000 sample 1: 45 tokens for exactly that.) So at r9-r10 the policy compressed to the minimal correct behavior (~30-46 tokens), reward 0.75 (3 aborted → 0, and maybe 1 failure).

Then r11: EVERYTHING went to "Okay" (2 tokens). The transition r10→r11 is the mystery. Two Adam steps on r10's data (steps 20-21), each with tiny grad_norm (3.3, 6.1), lr 5e-6 — and the policy completely flipped from ~75% correct 30-token trajectories to a deterministic 2-token "Okay"?

That doesn't add up for a healthy pipeline. A small-KL update cannot flip behavior so completely... unless the update was NOT small. ppo_kl at step 21: 0.066; train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff 0.0014. Those are per-token averages over the batch — could hide a catastrophic change on OTHER (unsampled) tokens. Actually KL on the sampled tokens is small, but the policy on the "LOOKUP" first tokens could have collapsed... no wait — the samples at r11 START with "Okay" — meaning P("Okay"-tokens | prompt) became dominant. But at r10, the samples started with "Okay, first..." too! (from Finish-rollout r10: "Okay, fi..."). So at r10 the model was already starting with "Okay". At r11 it starts with "Okay" and then... stops (im_end after 2 tokens? or "Okay" then no more?). Response = 2 tokens then the loop: text "Okay" has no LOOKUP, no FINAL → break after 1 turn. So the trajectory "Okay<im_end>" got reward 0.

So the policy at r10: "Okay, first request the ticket by writing LOOKUP: TR-xxx..." with ~30-46 tokens total and 75% success. At r11: "Okay" + EOS. The mass shifted from "Okay, first... LOOKUP" to just "Okay". Hmm, was the "Okay"-then-EOS mode present at r10? Maybe as a low-probability mode. For it to dominate at temp 0.8 in ALL 16 samples within 2 steps... The probability of continuing ", first request..." after "Okay" must have dropped below the probability of im_end. With tiny grad norms... suspicious.

Hmm, wait. Actually, let me reconsider. Maybe I should check the checkpoints! run.sh saves checkpoints every 4 rollouts (--save-interval 4) to $out/checkpoints.
